newsitem.title: FRANCE: Failed EU foreign policy needs reform -- Euro-MP.
newsitem.headline: Failed EU foreign policy needs reform -- Euro-MP.

text.p: A leading member of the European Parliament on Wednesday attacked the European Union's foreign policy record, urging EU leaders to adopt a more effective approach at their Amsterdam summit next week.

"The common foreign and security policy (CFSP)...is a story of institutional timidity and occasional failure of European solidarity under commercial pressures," Tom Spencer, the head of the EU assembly's foreign affairs committee, told Euro-MPs.

Spencer said the Maastricht treaty had given EU governments some ground rules for joint action on key foreign policy issues -- such as the Middle East peace process, the war in the former Yugoslavia and the genocide in Rwanda.
But the EU states had failed to use these powers properly, to the profound dismay of their public.
"They expected us to act to save lives and we failed," the British Conservative said.
EU leaders meet in Amsterdam next Monday and Tuesday to agree a package of wide-ranging reforms to the EU treaty which includes proposals for making the CFSP more effective.

Spencer, whose report on EU foreign policy successes and failures during 1996 is due to be adopted by the parliament on Thursday, urged European leaders to take a broader view than in the past and agree to act in unison on a wide range of issues.
"For a predominantly civilian superpower such as the Union, foreign policy is a mixture of trade and economics, environment and development, and security and human rights concerns."

The directly elected parliament has been pushing for the Amsterdam summit to give it more say in deciding EU foreign policy, a request which Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told Euro-deputies was likely to be met in part.
Spencer said he was an unapologetic enthusiast for parliamentary involvement and endorsed this move.
But he and other speakers in the CFSP debate cautioned Euro-MPs to be more critical of their own reactions to events and restrain their tendency to "shoot from the hip".
Hans van den Broek, the European Commissioner responsible for EU external policy, said he hoped the Amsterdam summit would give the EU "a true chance to be effective" on the world stage.
But he and many other speakers insisted that even these new, improved procedures would fail if EU governments continued to lack the political will to speak with one voice.

Among the EU's foreign policy failures last year, Spencer's report accuses the Union of an inability to react effectively to the implosion of Central Africa and the refugee crisis, or to events in the Middle East, Turkey, Lebanon, and Chechnya.
In other cases, such as China, Saudi Arabia and Algeria, the EU simply ignored problems of violence, human rights abuse, illegal arms exports and terrorism, the report continues.

The Union's record last year in the former Yugoslavia was better than during the height of the Balkan War, but EU policy there still lacks the direction needed to guide Bosnia- Herzogovina to elections in two years time, the report says.
